CheckTitle: Organization grants workflows a read-only default GITHUB_TOKEN
Description:
GitHub Actions organization settings define the default **GITHUB_TOKEN** permissions granted to every workflow run.

The evaluation determines whether the organization default is read-only, so that workflows have to opt in to write access through an explicit `permissions` block.
Risk:
A write-capable default **GITHUB_TOKEN** is available to every workflow in the organization, so any compromised step or dependency inherits it, leading to:
- Code integrity loss from pushed commits, moved tags, or altered releases
- Supply chain compromise when the token publishes packages or artifacts
- Weakened review controls when the token acts on pull requests and issues

Code.Other:
1. Sign in to GitHub as an organization owner
2. Go to your organization > Settings
3. In the left sidebar, click Actions > General
4. Under Workflow permissions, select Read repository contents and packages permissions
5. Click Save

Recommendation.Text:
Set the organization default **GITHUB_TOKEN** permissions to read-only and grant write scopes per workflow with an explicit `permissions` block, following **least privilege**.

Also prevent Actions from approving pull requests, and prefer short-lived **GitHub App** tokens over broad credentials when a workflow genuinely needs write access.
